rounds.text: Onix Solar Energy Ltd demonstrates exceptional top-line and bottom-line velocity, evidenced by a compounded sales growth of 463% and a compounded profit growth of 2071% over the trailing twelve months [E14, E15]. This explosive fundamental growth is beginning to manifest in market expectations, with profit growth exceeding one-year price growth by 2022% [E41]. The balance sheet offers robust downside protection, highlighted by an ultra-conservative debt-to-equity ratio of 0.07x [E27], comfortable short-term liquidity with a current ratio of 7.44x [E28], and a price-to-book ratio of 1.56x that trades attractively against the sector benchmark of 1.94x [E2, E7]. Insiders are heavily aligned with public shareholders, as promoter holding surged by 33.26 percentage points from December 2023 to 53.15% in September 2026, alongside an increase of 2.93% over the last quarter alone [E31, E44]. Furthermore, long-term investors have been rewarded through consistent multi-year share price appreciation, including a 111% gain over three years and 108% over five years [E17, E18]. Conceded: [E34] and [E35] indicate that a discounted cash flow model values the stock below its current market price with a negative margin of safety.

The valuation of Onix Solar Energy Ltd is disconnected from its fundamental cash generation, evidenced by a discounted cash flow intrinsic value of Rs 191 per share against a market price of Rs 328, resulting in a margin of safety of -71.8% [E34, E35]. This overvaluation is compounded by severe operational cash drain, with operating cash flow plunging to Rs -236 Cr and free cash flow mirroring this deficit in March 2026, leading to a distressed cash conversion ratio of -7.61x [E24, E25, E26]. Working capital conditions are deteriorating rapidly as high debtors stretch to 262 days and total working capital days balloon from 148 days to 494 days [E47, E48]. Furthermore, balance sheet risks are heightened by borrowings surging to Rs 57 Cr from zero a year prior alongside a concerning 94.5% pledge rate on promoter holdings [E29, E46]. These fundamental strains push the rules-based screen to a score of 39 out of 100 with a sell recommendation at medium confidence, driven by sharp year-over-year declines in net profit and sales alongside the profound DCF overvaluation [E49, E50, E51, E52]. Conceded: compounded sales growth reached 463% and compounded profit growth hit 2071% over the trailing twelve months [E14, E15].

Conceded: the discounted cash flow intrinsic value is Rs 191 per share against a market price of Rs 328 [E34, E35], operating cash flow and free cash flow reached Rs -236 Cr with a cash conversion of -7.61x [E24, E25, E26], working capital days expanded to 494 days alongside 262-day debtors [E47, E48], borrowings rose to Rs 57 Cr with a 94.5% promoter pledge rate [E29, E46], and the rules-based screen scored 39 out of 100 [E49, E50, E51, E52]. However, the bear's valuation claims overlook the strong fundamental growth momentum where compounded sales growth reached 463% and compounded profit growth hit 2071% over the trailing twelve months [E14, E15]. Profit growth exceeds one-year price growth by 2022%, signaling that the company is starting to outperform expectations [E41]. Furthermore, the balance sheet maintains a very conservative debt-to-equity ratio of just 0.07x alongside comfortable short-term liquidity with a current ratio of 7.44x [E27, E28, E43]. Promoter confidence is surging rather than retreating, shown by promoters increasing their holding by 33.26 percentage points overall since December 2023 and adding another 2.93% over the last quarter [E31, E44]. Finally, price-to-book of 1.51x trades below the sector benchmark of 1.94x [E7].

Conceded: compounded sales growth reached 463% and compounded profit growth hit 2071% over the trailing twelve months [E14, E15], promoters increased holdings by 33.26 percentage points overall since December 2023 and 2.93% over the last quarter [E31, E44], and price-to-book of 1.51x trades below the sector benchmark of 1.94x [E7]. However, pointing to headline growth numbers ignores the more recent sharp deterioration where net profit dropped 79% YoY and sales fell 69% YoY, triggering a poor rules-based screen score of 39 out of 100 [E49, E50, E51]. The claim of conservative leverage through a 0.07x debt-to-equity ratio [E27] completely bypasses the severe risk that 94.5% of promoter shares are pledged [E46], leaving the equity cushion highly vulnerable. Furthermore, citing strong short-term liquidity of 7.44x [E28] is undermined by the catastrophic reality that working capital days expanded to 494 alongside 262-day debtors [E47, E48], resulting in negative operating cash flow of Rs -236 Cr and a dismal cash conversion of -7.61x [E24, E25].
